title: Classifying spaces of weak equivalences in a model category
statement:
Use model categories and homotopy coherent localization as in [lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping], and nerves, spaces and cores as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category, with universes enlarged for all nerves below, and let $\mathcal S$ be a full subcategory closed under weak equivalences in both directions. Write $w\mathcal S$ for the category with the same objects and only weak equivalences as morphisms. Let $(\mathcal M_\infty)_{\mathcal S}$ be the full subcategory of the homotopy coherent localization on objects represented by $\mathcal S$. The localization functor induces a weak homotopy equivalence
$$N(w\mathcal S)\simeq\big((\mathcal M_\infty)_{\mathcal S}\big)^{\simeq}.$$
The superscript denotes the core, retaining precisely equivalences and their higher homotopies. Thus $\pi_0N(w\mathcal S)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of objects of $\mathcal S$ in $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)$, and the path space between two represented objects is the union of the equivalence components of their derived mapping space. Inclusions of the full cofibrant, full fibrant, and full bifibrant subcategories of $\mathcal S$, each with only weak equivalences as morphisms, induce weak homotopy equivalences on nerves.

Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be a Quillen adjunction between model categories, and let $\mathcal T$ be a full subcategory of $\mathcal N$ closed under weak equivalences in both directions. Suppose the adjunction is a Quillen equivalence, meaning its derived functors are inverse equivalences, and those derived functors carry the classes of objects represented by $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$ bijectively onto one another. It then induces a weak homotopy equivalence $N(w\mathcal S)\simeq N(w\mathcal T)$. On cofibrant objects it is induced by the left Quillen functor when that functor carries the chosen classes to one another, and on arbitrary objects it is computed after cofibrant replacement. These comparisons are natural for the Quillen functors and their derived units and counits.

source.place: Appendix A, classifying spaces of model categories: Proposition A.0.3 and Corollary A.0.4, printed pp. 207-209 (PDF pp. 213-215); the cofibrant/fibrant replacements give the nerve comparisons (compare Proposition A.0.6). These identify the components and equivalence path spaces, equivalently the core formulation stated here. Read online; absent locally. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: Put $C=w\mathcal S$ and $B=NC$, interpreted as a space by Kan replacement when necessary. Use [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice]. For $x\in C$, the image of $h_x$ under its left Quillen functor is $N(C/x)\to B$. The terminal object $(x,1_x)$ contracts $N(C/x)$: the arrow from $(z,u:z\to x)$ to $(x,1_x)$ is $u$. On nerves the contraction sends a chain to the chain with this final arrow appended. Its projection to $B$ is the corresponding homotopy to the vertex $x$. Thus $N(C/x)\to B$ is weakly equivalent, in the slice, to the vertex $x\to B$, via the inclusion of that terminal object. Consequently the derived slice mapping space from $N(C/y)$ to $N(C/x)$ is the path space $\operatorname{Path}_B(y,x)$. Here is a fibrant model even when the raw nerve $B$ is not Kan. Choose $r:B\to B^{\mathrm{Kan}}$. Write $K_0=B^{\mathrm{Kan}}$. The simplicial model structure on the slice in [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice] gives the Kan fibration $K_0^{\Delta^1}\to K_0^{\partial\Delta^1}=K_0\times K_0$: the simplicial lifting axiom applies to the cofibration $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the fibration $K_0\to *$. Restricting its final endpoint to $rx$ gives the path fibration $P_x\to B^{\mathrm{Kan}}$ of paths ending at $rx$, with projection the initial endpoint. Its total space contracts by precomposition with the nerve of $\max:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$: at the first parameter endpoint this is the identity path, at the second it is the constant path at $rx$, and the final endpoint stays $rx$. Pull it back to $B$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] the pullback has contractible total space, since its map to $P_x$ is a pullback of $r$ along that Kan fibration. Its map to $B$ is a fibration, and the constant path gives a weak equivalence from the vertex $x$. Its fiber at $y$ is $\operatorname{Path}_{B^{\mathrm{Kan}}}(ry,rx)$, which is precisely the derived slice mapping space from the vertex $y$ to the vertex $x$.

source.place: Proposition A.0.3, proof, first paragraph on printed p. 208: N(C/x) represents the vertex x in the slice

proof.text:
For $x\in\mathcal S$, [lem-coef-weak-equivalence-representable-local-model] supplies the actual local weak equivalence $h_x\to E_x$, with $E_x(y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{\mathrm{eq}}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qy,qx)$. The enriched evaluation and derived Quillen comparison of [lem-coef-locally-constant-presheaf-slice] therefore give
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\mathrm{eq}}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qy,qx)\simeq E_x(y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^{h}_{P_{\mathrm{lc}}(C)}(h_y,h_x)\simeq\operatorname{Path}_B(y,x).$$
All four terms refer to the same $x,y$ and the same $C$. The local-model unit sends an actual weak equivalence to its image under $q$, and the slice comparison sends its Yoneda morphism to the corresponding path in $NC$. Hence the inverse displayed equivalence is the map on paths induced by localization, including composition and its homotopies, rather than an unrelated equivalence of the two spaces.

source.place: Paragraph between Proposition A.0.3 and Corollary A.0.4, printed p. 208: the four-term mapping-space comparison

proof.text: Let $K=((\mathcal M_\infty)_{\mathcal S})^\simeq$. It is Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The actual localization map $NC\to K$ sends every arrow to an equivalence. Choose a Kan replacement $NC\to B^{\mathrm{Kan}}$. The universal groupoid-localization property [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] extends it to a map $a:B^{\mathrm{Kan}}\to K$ with its specified comparison on $NC$. The mapping spaces of $K$ are precisely the equivalence components of the ambient mapping spaces: its simplices retain exactly the equivalence edges and their higher simplices. Step 2 therefore says that $a$ induces an equivalence on every path space with endpoints represented by $\mathcal S$. Every component on each side contains such a vertex. Surjectivity on components follows; if two vertices have the same component in $K$, their path space there is nonempty, hence so is the path space in $B^{\mathrm{Kan}}$, proving injectivity. At a vertex $x$, taking $y=x$ in Step 2 identifies based loop spaces. Since $\pi_n(B,x)=\pi_{n-1}\operatorname{Path}_B(x,x)$ for $n\geq1$ (with the loop-group interpretation for $n=1$), it identifies every homotopy group. This is exactly weak homotopy equivalence. It also proves the claimed path-space formula. Components of the core are equivalence classes of objects; by [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] an edge of $\mathcal M_\infty$ is an equivalence exactly when its class is invertible in $h\mathcal M_\infty$, and $hq$ identifies $h\mathcal M_\infty$ with $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$. So components of the core are isomorphism classes of objects of $\mathcal S$ in $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)$, proving the $\pi_0$ formula as well.

source.place: Corollary A.0.4 and preceding path comparison, pp. 208-209; core reformulation and homotopy-group check written out

proof.text:
Choose a functorial cofibrant replacement $e:Q\to1$ by factoring the initial-object maps as cofibrations followed by trivial fibrations. Naturality gives $e_YQw=we_X$, so two-out-of-three makes $Qw$ a weak equivalence whenever $w$ is. Closure of $\mathcal S$ under weak equivalences makes $Q:w\mathcal S\to w\mathcal S_c$ well-defined. For the inclusion $i_c$, the restrictions of $e$ give $i_cQ\Rightarrow1$ and $Qi_c\Rightarrow1$, with components in the respective weak-equivalence categories. To see directly that their nerves are homotopies, for $\alpha:F\Rightarrow G$ the $j$th prism on $x_0\to\cdots\to x_n$ is
$$Fx_0\to\cdots\to Fx_j\xrightarrow{\alpha_{x_j}}Gx_j\to\cdots\to Gx_n\quad(0\leq j\leq n).$$
Naturality identifies the switching faces; deletion, composition and identity insertion give all other face and degeneracy equations. This is the homotopy of [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence], whose second clause, applied to these two transformations, makes $Ni_c$ and $NQ$ homotopy inverses.

source.place: Proposition A.0.6, proof of the left arrow, printed p. 209; explicit cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant replacement/prism argument

proof.text: Factor terminal-object maps functorially as trivial cofibrations $t_X:X\to TX$ followed by fibrations. Then $TX$ is fibrant, closure keeps it in $\mathcal S$, and $Tw\,t_X=t_Yw$ proves by two-out-of-three that $T$ preserves weak equivalences. For $i_f:w\mathcal S_f\to w\mathcal S$, restriction gives $1\Rightarrow i_fT$ and $1\Rightarrow Ti_f$. Apply the prism construction of Step 4 to these specified transformations: the switching arrow is $t_{x_j}:x_j\to Tx_j$, with the arrows before it unchanged and those after it mapped by $T$. This gives $1\simeq Ni_fNT$ and $1\simeq NTNi_f$, so $Ni_f$ is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence].

source.place: Proposition A.0.6, proof of the left arrow, printed p. 209; explicit cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant replacement/prism argument

proof.text: For a cofibrant $X$, the composite $0\to X\xrightarrow{t_X}TX$ is a cofibration. Indeed a lift against a trivial fibration is obtained first against $0\to X$ and then against $t_X$. Thus the fibrant replacement of Step 5 restricts to $T_c:w\mathcal S_c\to w\mathcal S_{cf}$. For the inclusion $j:w\mathcal S_{cf}\to w\mathcal S_c$, its replacement arrows give $1\Rightarrow jT_c$ and $1\Rightarrow T_cj$. All endpoints are cofibrant, all replacement targets are fibrant, and all components are weak equivalences. The prisms with switching arrows $t_{x_j}$ therefore lie in these specified categories and give inverse homotopies for $Nj$ and $NT_c$, by [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence]. Since the inclusion into $w\mathcal S$ is $i_cj$, Step 4 proves its nerve is also a homotopy equivalence. No model structure on a full cofibrant or fibrant subcategory is asserted.

source.place: Proposition A.0.6, proof of the left arrow, printed p. 209; explicit cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant replacement/prism argument

proof.text:
For $L\dashv R$, [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] supplies the coherent derived adjunction, computed on objects by $qLQ$ and $qRT$, and its actual derived unit and counit. By the Quillen-equivalence hypothesis these functors are inverse equivalences. If the hypothesis is read on ordinary homotopy categories, the derived adjunction's unit and counit are isomorphisms there, so their components are equivalences in the infinity categories (an edge is an equivalence exactly when its class is invertible, by [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category]); the same coherent transformations still give inverse infinity functors. The hypothesis on represented object classes restricts these inverse functors and their unit and counit to the full infinity subcategories represented by $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal T$. Taking cores restricts the same inverse transformations, so these cores are equivalent. Apply Steps 1-3 to the two model categories to get $N(w\mathcal S)\simeq N(w\mathcal T)$.

To identify the actual functor on nerves, $L$ preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects by the cited node. Hence, whenever $L$ carries the chosen cofibrant class into $\mathcal T$, it defines $w\mathcal S_c\to w\mathcal T$. Its square with the localization maps commutes, since the derived functor restricted to cofibrant objects is precisely localized $L$. The comparisons in Step 2 are induced by those maps, so this is the equivalence on nerves already constructed, using the cofibrant inclusion equivalence of Step 4 on the source. On arbitrary objects use $LQ$; its values lie in $\mathcal T$ because its derived values belong to the represented class: applying Steps 1–3 in the full target model category turns an equivalence to a represented object of $\mathcal T$ into a path in its weak-equivalence nerve, hence a finite zigzag of weak equivalences, all of whose vertices belong to $\mathcal T$ by closure. The natural comparison $Q\to1$ gives the replacement comparison. The actual derived unit and counit descend with their composition homotopies by the cited node; their restrictions and cores therefore give the asserted naturality. No arbitrary weak equivalence is passed through $L$ without first making its endpoints cofibrant.
